subject: ventures/bridal-hair-makeup-pricing-calculator

evidence.claims: Disclaimer (no warranty, not tax advice), no-upload privacy and DNT/GPC opt-out present and match usage.mjs. 'Exactly how many additional artists the schedule needs' (README.md:18, index.html:96 and JSON-LD :12, vs-flat-day-rate.html:40, vs-honeybook.html:46/:59, VENTURE.yaml:2) is false whenever looks cannot be packed (pack.mjs case: says 3, needs 4). vs-honeybook.html checked against the vendor where reachable: honeybook.com and marisstella.app were refused by the session proxy; a web search returned HoneyBook's own template URLs honeybook.com/templates/t/bridal-hair-makeup-pricing-guide and /bridal-hair-makeup-proposal, backing 'publishes its own Bridal Hair & Makeup Proposal and Pricing Guide templates'; 'smart file' combining proposal, contract and invoice and 'no free plan' are backed by third-party pricing guides (schedulingkit, agiled, assembly), not fetched from the vendor. The page itself says honeybook.com was not reachable and states no price, which is honest. 'Well documented as one of the industry-standard tools among bridal hair and makeup artists specifically' (vs-honeybook.html:39) has no source beyond the vendor publishing templates.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job: an artist quoting a bride + 6 bridesmaids at a 6am start, 50 miles out, with an assistant, sending a quote and taking a retainer. The tool gives the service total, early-start fee, travel and an extra-artist line, and makes the trial-credit discount visible, which is genuinely useful. It cannot produce the quote as artists write it: the early-start fee is flat per booking though vendors charge it per stylist ('$75 per stylist for start times between 5 am and 7 am' in one vendor list found by search), travel has no free radius and is not per artist, there is no retainer in 'balance due', no gratuity or service charge, no on-site touch-up hours, and no way to staff a separate hair stylist and makeup artist working in parallel, which is how most teams split a party. The staffing figure can be one artist short (correctness).
evidence.domain: Compared against published practice found by search (WeddingWire, The Knot, Glamsquad, vendor price lists): bridesmaid hair ~30-45 min and makeup ~30-45 min, so 'double those estimates' about 75-90 min for both, the bride 2-3 h; 10-15 min between people; early start $75-$200 before ~7am, often per stylist; mileage $0.75-$2/mi past a 15-25 mile radius; Knot averages about $300 bride and $210 per bridesmaid. Right: priced tiers, bride separate with extra time, buffer per person, early-start threshold, minimum top-up, extra-artist charge vs payout, trial credit as a discount. Departures: default 60 min for a one-artist hair+makeup look and 90 min for the bride sit below every source (with 90/120 min the default party needs 2 extra artists, not 1); staffing is pooled minutes, not a schedule; one-artist-does-both is the only staffing model; per-stylist fees and the free-mileage radius are not modelled; default prices are below the Knot averages (they are inputs, so low).

defects.what: Additional artists needed is pooled minutes / prep window, a lower bound that ignores indivisible looks; presented as 'exactly how many' it can be one artist short (bride 105 + 5 bridesmaids at 75, 10-min buffer, 180-min window: tool 3 artists, a real schedule needs 4). An artist staffing to it finds someone unfinished at the deadline.
'Exactly how many additional artists' is claimed in the README, the page FAQ and JSON-LD, both comparison pages and VENTURE.yaml, though the method is a pooled-minutes bound.

Quote lacks line items artists' contracts carry: early-start fee and travel per stylist (flat once regardless of extra artists), free-mileage radius, retainer in the balance due, gratuity or service charge, on-site touch-up hours; no separate hair-stylist and makeup-artist staffing.

Default timings (60 min for a one-artist hair+makeup look, 90 for the bride) are below published getting-ready guidance (about 30-45 min per service, doubled for both; bride 2-3 h) and uncited; the defaults understate staffing (1 extra artist vs 2 at 90/120).

Three seeded mutations survive 92 tests: net after payouts from the wedding-day total instead of contract value (only tested with the trial credited, where they are equal), the dollar minimum measured against service revenue alone (only tested with zero travel and early fee), kids dropped from the longest-look check.
vs-honeybook.html calls HoneyBook 'well documented as one of the industry-standard tools among bridal hair and makeup artists' with no source; only the vendor's own templates back the trade link.
A blank field passes validation as 0 (Number('') === 0): a cleared bride price silently drops $225 from the quote; capacity warning reads r.artistsBooked, which calculateQuote never returns.

verdict: The pricing arithmetic is right: defaults, a mixed six-tier party with two artists, a minimum top-up and the why-page worked example all recompute by hand to the cent, and the trial-credit-as-discount point is real and shown well. It does not meet the bar. The feature the venture leads with, how many artists the schedule needs, is pooled minutes over the window, so when looks cannot be packed it is an artist short while every page calls it exact; its default timings sit below published getting-ready guidance, which understates staffing further; the quote lacks per-stylist early-start and travel, a retainer, gratuity and touch-up time that a working artist's contract carries; and three of eight seeded mutations survive 92 passing tests. The HoneyBook page is mostly careful (it says it could not reach the vendor and gives no price) but adds an unsourced 'industry-standard' line. Correctness, verification, claims, fitness and domain are 2; completeness and craft 3.
